## Why This Is Asked
- Tests policy-driven drift protection across repos, not just data sharing.

## Key Concepts
- data.terraform_remote_state for policy bridge
- terraform plan -out and terraform show -json
- jq-based policy validation
- CI gating with environment scoping

## Code Example
```hcl
# policies.tf
data \"terraform_remote_state\" \"policies\" {
  backend = \"s3\"
  config  = {
    bucket = \"tf-policies-prod\"
    key    = \"drift/policies.tfstate\"
    region = \"us-east-1\"
  }
}
locals {
  allowed_changes = data.terraform_remote_state.policies.outputs[\"allowed_changes\"]
}
```

```bash
# CI gating (pseudo)
terraform init
terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan
terraform show -json plan.tfplan > plan.json
jq '.planned_changes' plan.json
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test this across multiple environments with different policy sets?
- How would you handle policy updates mid-PR?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to compose across repos and enforce read-only remotes. It checks multi-repo data sharing, and CI policy gates.

## Key Concepts
- data.terraform_remote_state usage
- module input wiring, outputs isolation
- CI gate enforcing drift/modify limits across remotes

## Code Example
```terraform
# app main
data "terraform_remote_state" "core" {
  backend = "s3"
  config = {
    bucket = "tf-core-network"
    key    = "prod/terraform.tfstate"
    region = "eu-west-1"
  }
}

module "app_vpc" {
  source   = "../../modules/app_vpc"
  vpc_cidr = data.terraform_remote_state.core.outputs.vpc_cidr
}
```

```yaml
# CI gate snippet (GitHub Actions)
- name: Plan app only
- run: terraform plan -out=plan.out -target=module.app
- run: terraform show -json plan.out > plan.json
- run: |
    if jq '.resource_changes[].address' plan.json | grep -qE 'core|aws_.*$'; then
      echo "Core-network changes detected"; exit 1; fi
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test in Terratest that read-only remote state is prevented from drift?
- How would you handle secret-backed outputs?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This evaluates your ability to design a disaster recovery pattern across regions with strict isolation. It tests using remote state as a read-only data bridge, implementing per-environment backends, and creating CI gates to prevent accidental modifications to primary infrastructure.

## Key Concepts

- Cross-region isolation using Terraform remote state
- Provider aliasing for primary region access
- Per-environment backend configuration
- Read-only data consumption versus resource creation
- CI/CD gatekeeping for protection

## Code Example

```hcl
# Data bridge (DR repo)

terraform {
  backend "s3" {
    bucket = "dr-terraform-state"
    key    = "network/terraform.tfstate"
    region = "us-west-2"
  }
}

provider "aws" {
  alias  = "primary"
  region = "us-east-1"
}

data "terraform_remote_state" "primary_vpc" {
  backend = "s3"
  config = {
    bucket = "primary-terraform-state"
    key    = "network/terraform.tfstate"
    region = "us-east-1"
  }
}

# Read-only consumption of primary resources
locals {
  primary_vpc_id = data.terraform_remote_state.primary_vpc.outputs.vpc_id
  primary_subnets = data.terraform_remote_state.primary_vpc.outputs.private_subnets
}

# DR resources only (no primary region resources)
resource "aws_vpc" "dr_vpc" {
  cidr_block = "10.20.0.0/16"
}
```

## CI/CD Gate Logic

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# CI gate to prevent primary region modifications

terraform plan -out=tfplan

# Check if any resources would be created/modified in primary region
if terraform show -json tfplan | jq -r '.planned_values.root_module.resources[] | select(.provider_name == "aws.primary") | .address' | grep -q .; then
  echo "ERROR: Plan contains changes in primary region (us-east-1)"
  echo "Changes found:"
  terraform show -json tfplan | jq -r '.planned_values.root_module.resources[] | select(.provider_name == "aws.primary") | "- \(.address)"'
  exit 1
fi

echo "✓ No primary region changes detected. Plan approved."
terraform apply tfplan
```

## Implementation Notes

- Primary repo exports VPC data via outputs
- DR repo only reads state data, never creates primary region resources
- Provider alias ensures correct region targeting
- CI gate parses JSON plan to detect any primary region changes
- State isolation through separate S3 backends per region
